literal: Subordinate to the Zhongjing regent's office.
idiomatic: It answered to the Zhongjing regent.

literal: Ze Prefecture was set up in Kaitai.
idiomatic: Kaitai established Ze Prefecture.

literal: There are Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong Ridge, Shizi Ridge, the Luo River, and the Sa River.
idiomatic: Landmarks include Songting Pass, Spirit Mountain, Jiugong and Shizi ridges, the Luo River, and the Sa River.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing two counties:
idiomatic: Two counties:

literal: Shenshan County.
idiomatic: Shenshan County.

literal: Spirit Mountain lies to the southwest.
idiomatic: Spirit Mountain stands in the southwest.

literal: Luanhe County.
idiomatic: Luanhe County.

literal: Originally Han Xuwu County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Xuwu County land.

literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.
idiomatic: Under Yongxing Palace.

literal: Bei'an Prefecture, Xinghua Army, upper grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Bei'an Prefecture—Xinghua Army, upper grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Nuqi County territory, belonging to Shanggu Commandery.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Nuqi County in Shanggu Commandery.

literal: Under Jin it was seized by Feng Ba.
idiomatic: Jin times saw Feng Ba take it.

literal: Under Tang it was western territory of the Xi princely mansion.
idiomatic: Tang made it the Xi princely house's western domain.

literal: Shengzong settled Han households to establish Bei'an Prefecture.
idiomatic: Shengzong placed Han households and founded Bei'an Prefecture.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county: Xinghua County.
idiomatic: One county: Xinghua County.

literal: Originally Han Qieju County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Qieju County land.

literal: Tan Prefecture, Guangrun Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Tan Prefecture—Guangrun Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Longshan County of Zhongjing; the prefecture was set up in Kaitai and remained under Zhongjing.
idiomatic: It was Zhongjing's Longshan County; Kaitai made it a prefecture still under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county: Longshan County.
idiomatic: One county: Longshan County.

literal: Originally Han Jiaoli County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Jiaoli County ground.

literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Xijia Stockade.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it from Xijia Stockade.

literal: Songshan Prefecture, Sheng'an territory, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Songshan Prefecture—Sheng'an territory, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Established in Kaitai.
idiomatic: Created in Kaitai.

literal: Abolished in Tonghe year 8, then restored.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8 abolished it; later it was restored.

literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: Under Zhongjing.

literal: Governing one county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Songshan County.
idiomatic: Songshan County.

literal: Originally Han Wencheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Wencheng County land.

literal: Bordering Songmo, a merchant crossroads.
idiomatic: On the Songmo frontier, a hub of trade.

literal: Established as a county in Kaitai year 2.
idiomatic: Made a county in Kaitai year 2.

literal: There is the Song Mountain stream.
idiomatic: The Song Mountain river runs through it.

literal: Song minister Wang Zeng's Account of Presenting Matters to the Khitan says: leaving Yanjing's north gate, one reaches Wangjing Hostel.
idiomatic: Wang Zeng's Account of Service to the Khitan records: from Yanjing's north gate to Wangjing Hostel,

literal: fifty li to Shun Prefecture.
idiomatic: fifty li to Shun Prefecture;

literal: seventy li to Tan Prefecture, gradually entering mountains.
idiomatic: seventy li to Tan Prefecture as the road climbs into hills;

literal: fifty li to Jingou Hostel.
idiomatic: another fifty li reaches Jingou Hostel.

literal: Approaching the hostel, the river plain opens wide—called the Jingou shoals.
idiomatic: Near the hostel the valley floor widens into what they call the Jingou flats.

literal: From here one enters the mountains, winding up steep paths; there are no more mile markers—only days on horseback estimate the distance.
idiomatic: Beyond lies twisting mountain grades without mileposts; travelers count days on horseback to reckon distance.

literal: Ninety li to Gubeikou; steep cliffs on both sides barely admit a cart track.
idiomatic: Ninety li brings Gubeikou, where cliffs on both sides admit only a single cart track.

literal: Crossing Desheng Ridge with its layered switchbacks—folk name Homesick Ridge—eighty li to Xin Hostel.
idiomatic: Desheng Ridge's switchbacks, known as Homesick Ridge, lead eighty li to Xin Hostel.

literal: Passing Diaoke Ridge and Pianqiang Ridge, forty li to Wolai Hostel.
idiomatic: Past Diaoke and Pianqiang ridges, forty li to the Reclining Tathagata Hostel.

literal: Crossing the Wuluan River—with Luan Prefecture to the east—then Modou Ridge, also called Duyun Ridge and Qincai Ridge; seventy li to Liuhe Hostel.
idiomatic: The Wuluan River is crossed with Luan Prefecture eastward; Modou Ridge, alias Duyun and Qincai ridges, lies seventy li before Liuhe Hostel.

literal: Songting Ridge is very precipitous; seventy li to the Forging Tribes Hostel.
idiomatic: Songting Ridge is sheer; seventy li farther stands the Forging Tribes Hostel.

literal: Southeast fifty li to Niushan Hostel.
idiomatic: Fifty li southeast to Niushan Hostel.

literal: Eighty li to Lu'er Gorge Hostel.
idiomatic: Eighty li to Deer Gorge Hostel.

literal: Crossing Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Tiejiang Hostel.
idiomatic: Over Hamo Ridge, ninety li to Iron-Slurry Hostel.

literal: Crossing Shizi Ridge, from here gradually leaving the mountains, seventy li to Fugu Hostel.
idiomatic: Shizi Ridge passed, the road slowly descends from the hills; seventy li to Fugu Hostel.

literal: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, twenty li to Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture.
idiomatic: Eighty li to Tongtian Hostel, then twenty li to Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.

literal: The walls are low and small; the circuit barely four li square.
idiomatic: Walls are low and the city circuit scarcely four li around.

literal: Gates are only layered roofs, without tower-gate construction.
idiomatic: Gatehouses are stacked roofs without barbican towers.

literal: The south gate is called Zhuxia; within the gate connected walking corridors and many ward gates.
idiomatic: The south gate Zhuxia opens on covered walkways and many lane gates.

literal: There are also four market towers: called Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.
idiomatic: Four market towers stand: Tianfang, Daqu, Tonghuan, and Wangque.

literal: Next one reaches Datong Hostel.
idiomatic: Farther on lies Datong Hostel.

literal: Its gate due north is called Yangde and Changge.
idiomatic: Its north-facing gate bears the names Yangde and Changge.

literal: Within the city on a hillock in the southwest corner is a temple.
idiomatic: A temple crowns a southwest hill inside the walls.

literal: South of the city are gardens, a place for banquets and archery.
idiomatic: South of the walls lie gardens used for feasts and archery.

literal: From passing Gubeikou, inhabitants live in thatched huts and plank houses and farm, but there is no mulberry or catalpa;
idiomatic: Beyond Gubeikou people dwell in thatch huts and plank houses and till fields, yet plant no mulberry or catalpa;

literal: all planting is on ridge crests, lest blown sand bury the crops.
idiomatic: crops are sown on ridge tops for fear windblown sand would bury them.

literal: In the mountains tall pines grow dense; deep valleys sometimes show pastured cattle, horses, and camels—many blue sheep and yellow swine.
idiomatic: Mountains hold thick pine; valleys often show cattle, horses, and camels, with many blue sheep and yellow hogs.

literal: Cheng Prefecture, Xingfu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Cheng Prefecture—Xingfu Army, military commissioner.

literal: The Jin state's Senior Princess established it with dowry households; the army was called Changqing, subordinate to Shangjing.
idiomatic: The Jin Senior Princess founded it with dowry households under the Changqing army, subordinate to Shangjing.

literal: The army name was changed again.
idiomatic: The army designation was later renamed.

literal: Governing one county: Tongchang County.
idiomatic: One county: Tongchang County.

literal: Xingzhong Prefecture.
idiomatic: Xingzhong Prefecture.

literal: Originally Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Formerly Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army), military commissioner.

literal: The ancient Guzhu state.
idiomatic: Land of ancient Guzhu.

literal: Han Liucheng County territory.
idiomatic: Han Liucheng County ground.

literal: Murong Huang, taking the land north of Liucheng and south of Long Mountain as a place of fortune and virtue, built Long City, erected palaces and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng County, moved the capital, and styled it Helong Palace.
idiomatic: Murong Huang deemed the tract between Liucheng and Long Mountain auspicious, built Long City with palaces and shrines, renamed Liucheng Longcheng County, moved the capital, and called it Helong Palace.

literal: Murong Chui dwelt there again; later it was destroyed by Northern Yan.
idiomatic: Murong Chui returned there; Northern Yan later destroyed it.

literal: Northern Wei took it as Liaoxi Commandery.
idiomatic: Northern Wei made it Liaoxi Commandery.

literal: Sui pacified Gao Baoning and set up Ying Prefecture.
idiomatic: Sui subdued Gao Baoning and established Ying Prefecture.

literal: Emperor Yang abolished the prefecture and set up Liucheng Commandery.
idiomatic: Sui Yang-di abolished the prefecture for Liucheng Commandery.

literal: Early Tang Wude changed it to Ying Prefecture chief commandery, soon a protectorate headquarters.
idiomatic: Early Tang Wude made it Ying chief command, soon a protectorate seat.

literal: In Wansui Tongtian it fell to Li Wanrong.
idiomatic: Wansui Tongtian saw it lost to Li Wanrong.

literal: Early Shenlong moved the headquarters to Youzhou.
idiomatic: Early Shenlong shifted the seat to Youzhou.

literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored administration at Liucheng.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 4 returned government to Liucheng.

literal: Year 8 it moved west to Yuyang.
idiomatic: Year 8 the seat moved west to Yuyang.

literal: Year 10 it returned to Liucheng.
idiomatic: Year 10 brought it back to Liucheng.

literal: Later the Xi seized it.
idiomatic: The Xi later held it.

literal: Taizu pacified the Xi and captured Yan households; intending to build a city, he ordered Han Zhifang to choose the site.
idiomatic: Taizu subdued the Xi, took Yan captives, and charged Han Zhifang to choose a city site.

literal: Liucheng was then repaired and styled Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.
idiomatic: Liucheng was rebuilt as Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army) with a military commissioner.

literal: In Tonghe times the frontier commission of Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan five prefectures was set up.
idiomatic: Tonghe created a frontier commission over Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan prefectures.

literal: Soon the commission was abolished; it was subordinate to Jiqing Palace.
idiomatic: The commission was soon dropped and the seat joined Jiqing Palace.

literal: Later it belonged to Xingsheng Palace.
idiomatic: Later it passed to Xingsheng Palace.

literal: Chongxi year 10 it was promoted to Xingzhong Prefecture.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 10 elevated it to Xingzhong Prefecture.

literal: There are Great Huashan, Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk-fragrance Cliff—with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's carved stone—Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.
idiomatic: It boasts Great and Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk Cliff with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's inscription, Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.

literal: Two prefectures, four counties:
idiomatic: It governed two prefectures and four counties:

literal: Xingzhong County.
idiomatic: Xingzhong County.

literal: Originally Han Liucheng County territory.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Liucheng County land.

literal: Taizu plundered Han households to dwell here and built Bacheng County.
idiomatic: Taizu settled plundered Han households and founded Bacheng County.

literal: In Chongxi the prefecture was set up and the name changed.
idiomatic: Chongxi established the prefecture and renamed the county.

literal: Yingqiu County.
idiomatic: Yingqiu County.

literal: Split off from Bacheng.
idiomatic: Carved from Bacheng.

literal: Xianglei County.
idiomatic: Xianglei County.

literal: Established in Kaitai year 2 from Maiwu River.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 2 founded it on the Maiwu River.

literal: First subordinate to Zhongjing.
idiomatic: First under Zhongjing.

literal: Later subordinate.
idiomatic: Later subordinate.

literal: Lüshan County.
idiomatic: Lüshan County.

literal: Originally Han Qielü County.
idiomatic: Formerly Han Qielü County.
